results.summary: An explicit finite size guarantee gives single-use and two-use bounds for the same channel, and hence a quantitative additivity gap.
The rate defined using physical codes equals the regularized Holevo information; the equality is proved rather than used as a definition.
The prescribed channel has a capacity advantage over its single-use Holevo information that grows with the block parameter.
For each fixed K, the asymptotic two-use information per use is at least a specified multiple of the single-use information.
One finite channel can simultaneously have tiny positive single-use information, a large capacity gain, and a large two-use ratio.
A separate deterministic construction realizes the qualitative bounds for every allowed block length, without a prescribed local-size formula.
A sequence of actual channels has single-use information tending to zero and two-use information per use, and capacity, diverging.
With K fixed and a positive gap coefficient, the gap is linear in output cost and proportional to the square root of input cost.
The exact integer-rounded input dimension has an asymptotic qubit-cost expansion, including its constant term.
Normalize the proved gap by output qubits and quantify how its guaranteed fraction depends on K.
Regrouping more and more uses of one fixed channel cannot produce a persistent linear two-block gap.
A growing-K family makes single-use information vanish while two-use information and capacity grow, with explicit input-qubit costs.
The free-group comparison bounds an operator norm by a Hilbert–Schmidt coefficient norm, setting the scale for the channel certificate.
A finite Haar expectation estimate and net selection yield a uniform adjoint bound at the specified dimensions.
An adjoint norm bound implies a purity and entropy bound for every output density matrix.
An explicit Bell input gives a joint output entropy deficit for the complementary channel and its conjugate.
At every positive tensor power, the Weyl extension turns minimum output entropy into an exact Holevo quantity.
One finite-set factorization works uniformly across the admissible Hilbert-space representations and transfers approximation errors.
Weighted chronological counting proves the sharper one-pair Haar estimate at the original dimension threshold.
An expectation bound provides an explicit positive probability of a favorable finite realization.
The correct exploration budget is defect plus two; a formal counterexample explains why the extra event is necessary.
Marked positions and the repaired coefficient exponent replace an invalid intermediate run count.
A stronger undamped realization in every sufficiently large dimension remains outside the proved endpoints.
The library defines general convergence interfaces, while the completed construction uses specialized proved finite estimates.
Some broader background formulations extend beyond the coefficient models and coding results formalized here.
